finding.claim: Decrypted plaintext secret is logged at Trace level, violating the org policy against logging sensitive data at any level.
finding.source: Encrypted config value matching {cipher}... from any configuration source (DecryptionConfigurationProvider.cs:29-31)
finding.sink: LogDecrypt(key, value, decryptedValue) with a LoggerMessage at Trace that includes PlainTextValue (lines 58-59)

trace.note: Plaintext passed to LogDecrypt whenever the value changes

finding.guards_checked: Only the Trace log level gates the write. No redaction of the plaintext argument. Impact requires Trace logging for the Steeltoe.Configuration category and access to log output. Not a remote-attacker path.

finding.claim: Cloud Foundry actuator authorization matches the raw request path. A dot-segment path such as /cloudfoundryapplication/health/../env might pass the health match, which requires no permission, while the router resolves it to the env endpoint. Unverified: depends on whether ASP.NET routing normalizes dot segments.
finding.source: HTTP request path with dot segments, e.g. /cloudfoundryapplication/health/../env
finding.sink: Protected endpoint env (RequiredPermissions Full, EnvironmentEndpointOptions.cs:16) served without a permission check

trace.note: StartsWithSegments on the raw path selects the endpoint for permission checks
Request then passes to the next middleware/router, which may normalize the path

finding.guards_checked: Trailing-slash and case variants are covered by StartsWithSegments. The repo has no dot-segment handling and no test for it. Confirming requires running the app and checking ASP.NET routing normalization. Severity depends on that result; the exposed endpoints require Full permissions.

finding.claim: The root CA private key is written as an unprotected PFX (no password) into a directory shared by projects, and the leaf private key is written as plaintext PEM with default file permissions.
finding.source: Local filesystem; no attacker input. The attacker is another local user or process that can read the parent directory.
finding.sink: File.WriteAllBytes(RootCaPfxPath, caCertificate.Export(Pfx)) at line 62; File.WriteAllText(...Key.pem, keyContents) at line 100

trace.note: Root CA path is in the parent directory, shared across projects
Root CA PFX written without a password
Leaf private key written as plaintext PEM with default umask permissions

finding.guards_checked: Code runs only outside Cloud Foundry. No password, no explicit file mode, no restriction on the parent directory. Impact is local-only (dev machines or shared hosts): anyone who reads the CA key can mint certificates trusted by apps that trust SteeltoeGeneratedCA. Lower severity.
